summary: Naoki Nabeshima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who founded Ryukoku University and served there as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).

Naoko Nishimura is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD at Tohoku University (1993–2002) under Toshifumi Goto, Hirofumi Isoda, and Shinkan Murakami, and later served there as a specialized researcher (attested 2026).

Appleton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. After completing her D.Phil. at Oxford under Christopher Minkowski and David Gellner, she was a postdoctoral fellow at Cardiff and became a professor and co-director at Edinburgh.
Naomichi Nakada is an Indologist and philosopher who completed his doctoral studies under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and also studied under Ram Chandra Pandeya.

Tsuji studied at the University of Tokyo (Bungaku Hakushi) and Oxford under Macdonell, Fraser, Geldner, and Lévi. A linguist and Indologist, he was Associate Professor and Chair of Sanskrit at Tokyo and director at Toyo Bunko.
Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions as a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and at Otani University (attested 1981).

Narada Maha Thera was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at St. Benedict's College and University College, Colombo. He served as Superior at Vajirarama, Colombo, from around 1962 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961) under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (circa 1961–1984).
Narayan Sastri Khiste was an Indology scholar who served as librarian (adhyaksha) at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1932) and later as Principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1950).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology who held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from around 1967 to 1999.

Narendrachandra Bhattacharyya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series (attested 1936) and as a Pandit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indology and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Calcutta (PhD 1985). He held positions at Kobe University and served as Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1995–2010).
Narimoto Tamayama was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1974 and 1988).

Philosopher Natalie Depraz studied at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre. She held posts at the Collège International de Philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne, Galatasaray, and the University of Rouen Normandy, where she founded the Rouen School of Phenomenology.
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held an affiliation at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1972–1975) under Stephan V. Beyer, having also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan (1999–2006) and took up a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After receiving her PhD from Harvard (2005), she held positions at UC Berkeley, UCLA as Assistant Professor, and the University of Virginia as faculty.

Natasha Reichle is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indology scholar who completed her PhD under Hans T. Bakker and held an academic post at the University of Groningen from circa 2011 to 2018.
